prose.headline: AGNT is a buy at $4.08 for $4.78 by Nov 2; a daily close under $3.94 ends it.
story: AGNT snapped out of a falling wedge on Oct 8 at $3.75 and today jumped 9.5% to $4.08, printing a full-bodied bullish marubozu straight off the 50-day at $3.98, which it reclaimed on the close. The spring on Sep 25, a dip under the prior low that was bought back within three sessions, marked the floor, and the support zone at $3.81 to $3.96 sits just beneath. This is still a beaten-down chart: a 72% collapse from the $12.23 52-week high to the $3.40 low, with price under a falling 200-day at $5.64 and under the 10-month line at $5.45, so the bigger picture remains a weekly downtrend.

The turn has real momentum behind it. RSI jumped to 57 from 47, and MACD, still a hair below zero, has moved back above its signal line, with a bullish divergence on MACD and on the accumulation line. Turnover ran 1.10× normal today and 1.15× over ten sessions, steady rather than heavy. Over the past month it has outrun SPY by 6.5 points, and buyers since the Aug 4 earnings report are back in profit above $3.94. Revenue grew 10.7% while the loss widened slightly to $2.7M. The daily and hourly trends have turned up even as the weekly trend still points down, in a choppy market with the VIX calm at 17. A small company bouncing off a reclaimed average, with a clean line right below.

prose.headline: Park Hotels: buy the last session's low at $16.11, run to $17.21 by Nov 2; wrong below $15.87.
story: Park Hotels climbed 2.9% to $16.57 on volume of 1.37× normal, closing over its last swing high at $16.20 and pressing its 52-week high of $16.63, with the weekly swing high at $16.77 one step above. The breakout has a clean base under it: the 20-day at $15.48 and the 50-day at $15.39 were reclaimed together on Oct 15 and held, the 10-day at $15.58 is rising, and the 200-day at $13.01 sits far below. The top of the high-volume range at $15.87 is the line the breakout cannot lose, with the busiest price of the month at $15.19 beneath it.

MACD crossed up on Oct 15 and is above zero with the gap widening, RSI rose to 70 from 64, and hidden bullish divergences on RSI, MACD and money flow show each dip has been bought harder. ADX at 17 says the trend is still building rather than tired. The turnaround is real: profit was $47.0M against a $5.0M loss a year earlier, and holders since the Aug 6 earnings report average $15.34. The stock is 15.9 points ahead of real estate over three months, and heavy short interest adds fuel if the old high gives way. October has a weak record for the name, and the desk already holds it. A shallow dip is the entry.

prose.headline: Insperity: buy now at $49.49 to $50.02, upside to $54.94 by Oct 29; void below $48.46.
story: Insperity bounced 2.0% to $50.02 off its 20-day average, which held its retest on Oct 19 at $48.46, with an inside bar and bullish harami forming at the 50-day. That 50-day at $50.21 was lost the same day and is the line to retake, and the earnings average since the Jul 29 report at $50.58 sits just above, so holders from that report are slightly under water. The busiest price at $50.65 is in the same pocket. Below, a support line near $48.14 and the support zone from $47.82 to $48.46 form the floor, and the spring on Oct 6 that undercut the 40-day low and recovered marked the low of this swing.

Momentum is turning back up: RSI climbed to 53 from 49 and MACD has moved above zero and over its signal line. ADX at 12 says there is no trend on the daily yet, and RSI has diverged against the recent highs, so this is a range trade toward the top until the 50-day is reclaimed. The bigger trend favors the long: the six-month gain of 57% tops 95% of stocks, the 200-day at $39.21 is far below, and the weekly chart is in markup. The business turned a profit of $4.0M from a $5.0M loss a year earlier. A close back over $50.65 opens the run to the weekly swing high.

prose.headline: Comstock: long on a pullback into $13.38, upside target $14.85 by Nov 2; a close below $13.22 kills it.
story: Comstock is trying to turn a weekly downtrend into a base. The stock lost 57% from its $28.10 52-week high to the $12.12 low, the spring on Oct 1 shook out the bottom, and since then the swings have turned higher. Today it eased 0.8% to $14.12 after retesting the 50-day at $13.91 and holding, two sessions after the 20-day at $13.44 did the same. The support zone from $13.38 to $13.72 sits right under that, with the busiest price of the month at $13.63. The ceiling of the range is clear: the top of the high-volume range at $14.85, then the weekly swing high at $15.22, while the 200-day at $16.47 still falls.

Momentum flipped first. MACD crossed above zero on Oct 16 and sits above its signal line, RSI is at 56, and the accumulation line, money flow and MACD all show bullish divergences off the low, while on-balance volume rises with price. Volume is calm, 0.76× normal today. The business is the drag: revenue fell 24.9% and profit dropped to $8.8M from $124.8M, so the move is a trade, not a turnaround story. Heavy short interest adds fuel if the range top gives way, energy leads the sector map, and the stock has outrun SPY by 9.0 points this month. Holders since the Jul 29 earnings report average $13.91, right at the 50-day. A base with real support under it and a defined top.

prose.headline: National Presto: buy $145.86 on the dip, target $153.83 by Oct 29; wrong under $144.54.
story: National Presto slipped 0.8% to $149.25 on volume of 1.66× normal, printing a pin bar and spinning top at a recent swing high, a rejection that points to a dip first. Underneath, the averages caught it today: the 20-day at $148.30 and the 50-day at $148.50 both held their retests, and the 10-day sits at $148.76, all bunched within about a dollar. The high-volume range runs from $144.54 to $153.83 with the busiest price at $151.66, so the stock is trading in the middle of its own value. A support zone from $141.90 to $145.90 backs the lower edge, and the 200-day at $135.40 rises well below.

The chart is coiled. The bands sit in the narrowest fifth of the year and ADX reads 10, a squeeze that usually resolves with a sharp move. RSI is neutral at 52 and MACD sits above zero but below its signal line, while a hidden bullish divergence on the MACD momentum bars favors an upside release. Relative strength carries the case: the stock is 28.4 points ahead of its industrials sector and 18.8 points ahead of the S&P 500 over three months. Revenue grew 21.7% and profit climbed to $15.9M from $5.2M, and holders since the Aug 3 earnings report average $147.20. The 52-week high of $158.17 is the bigger prize once the range top gives way.

prose.headline: Phibro Animal Health is a long from $37.70 toward $40.65 by Oct 30, out below $37.24.
story: Phibro Animal Health slipped 1.4% to $38.80 after an engulfing reversal bar with a wick rejection at its 20-session high, the kind of bar that usually brings a dip back into support. That support is close: the zone from $37.70 to $38.72 sits right under price, the 10-day is at $38.05, and the top of the high-volume range is $38.51. Further down, the 20-day at $36.84, reclaimed Oct 1, and the 50-day at $36.30, which held its retest Oct 7, back it up, with the busiest price at $35.89. The weekly swing high at $40.65 is the target, and the falling 200-day at $41.29 is the heavier wall above it.

This is a recovery, not a leader yet. The stock is only at 65% of its 52-week high of $60.08 and down 28% over six months, but it has run 11.9 points ahead of the S&P 500 over three months as health care leads the sector map. RSI eased to 61 from 65 and MACD holds above zero and its signal line; ADX at 21 marks a young trend, and hidden bullish divergences on RSI, MACD and the accumulation line say the dips are being bought. Revenue grew 10.3% with profit at $24.0M against $20.9M, holders since the Aug 26 earnings report average $36.70, and October has a strong record for the stock. the desk's strategy bought it today.

prose.headline: Macerich is a dip buy at $22.74 by Oct 23, toward $25.72 by Nov 23; void under $22.55.
story: Macerich jumped 3.2% to $23.24 and took back both its 20-day at $22.64 and its 50-day at $23.23 in a single session, on volume of 1.12× normal. That move sits on a solid base: the spring on Oct 8 undercut the 40-day low at $22.00 and snapped back, the 10-day at $22.57 has turned up, the 200-day at $22.01 rises underneath, and the 38.2% Fibonacci retrace of the whole advance sits at $22.61. The support zone from $22.55 to $22.88 gathers those levels into one floor. The ceiling is far off, with the weekly swing high at $25.97 and the 52-week high of $26.68.

RSI jumped to 55 from 46 and MACD has turned up over its signal line while still below zero, an early turn, and the daily chart printed a fresh buy mark. ADX at 22 shows a trend starting. The weekly chart is the caution: it still looks like a topping pattern, the stock trails the S&P 500 by 11.3 points over three months, and volume flow has not confirmed the bounce. Holders since the Aug 4 earnings report average $23.40, so the first supply sits just above. The loss narrowed to $27.1M from $40.9M, and heavy short interest can push a squeeze once that supply clears. The desk already holds it.

prose.headline: Newell Brands: buy now at $5.62 to $5.68, aim for $6.13 by Oct 28; out under $5.54.
story: Newell Brands rose 2.5% to $5.68 and closed near the high, reclaiming its 20-day average at $5.54 today with a piercing line at the bottom of the high-volume range. The swings have climbed with higher highs and higher lows since the spring on Oct 1 undercut the 40-day low at $5.21 and snapped back. The 20-day, the support line and the 20-day volume-weighted price all sit together at $5.54, one clear line to lean on. The work is overhead: a resistance zone from $5.72 to $5.86 and the 50-day at $5.79, lost on Sep 23, are the first lid, with the busiest price of the month up at $6.18.

RSI rose to 52 from 47, and MACD is below zero but back above its signal line, so momentum is improving from a low base, and the hourly chart printed a fresh buy mark. Volume was light at 0.74× normal, so the move still needs sponsors. Holders since the Jul 31 earnings report average $5.92 and are trapped, a supply zone above. prose.headline: Ameren's dip to $104.68 is a long toward $108.60 by Oct 30, wrong below $103.70.
story: Ameren climbed 2.1% to $106.23, closing near the high and back over its 50-day at $104.50 for the first time since the summer. The 20-day at $101.80 held its retest on Oct 9 and the 10-day at $103.76 is rising underneath, and the spring on Oct 1 that undercut the 40-day low marked the low of the drop, with a support line near $98.29. The pullback zone lines up with the deepest Fibonacci retrace of the year's advance at $104.90 and the support zone from $104.80 to $106.90. Holders since the Jul 30 earnings report average $104.53 and are back in profit.

Momentum confirms the turn: RSI rose to 61 from 54, MACD crossed above zero on Oct 16 and sits above its signal line with the gap widening, ADX at 26 shows a real trend, and the daily chart printed a buy mark. The bigger picture is a bounce inside a weekly downtrend, with the 200-day at $108.10 and the 10-month average at $108.24 both overhead and weekly MACD diverging, so the trade aims at the resistance zone from $108.60 to $109.70 and not beyond. The stock sits at 90% of its 52-week high of $118.32, so there is room once that zone clears.

prose.headline: ArcBest: sell a failed bounce into $133.70, target $124.06 by Nov 2; a close over $134.79 kills it.
story: ArcBest lost its 50-day back on Jul 29 and has not owned it since; that average now sits at $133.70 and keeps falling. Today's 1.4% lift to $129.99 put price back over the 20-day at $129.40. Directly above sits a resistance zone from $134.50 to $138.00, and buyers since the Jul 29 earnings report average $136.08 and are trapped. On the weekly chart price is under both the 10-week and 30-week lines. The stock has surrendered a big piece of its run from $59.43 to $176.70, and the 38.2% Fibonacci level at $131.90 is the first shelf the rebound has to clear.

Momentum is trying, on very little fuel. RSI rose to 48 from 44 and MACD is back above its signal line but still below zero, while turnover ran just 0.46× normal today and 0.79× across ten sessions. On-balance volume keeps falling with price. Relative strength is poor, 21.3 points behind the S&P 500 over three months in an industrials sector near the bottom of the map, and a $13.8M loss replaced a $25.8M profit even as revenue rose 15.9%. The one real argument against is today's bullish engulfing candle at the bottom of the high-volume range, a buyer's footprint at $128.35. A quiet bounce into a falling average with a wall of trapped buyers overhead is a place to sell, not to chase.

prose.headline: Celsius is a long at $29.96 for $33.31 by Nov 2, invalid on a daily close below $29.36.
story: Celsius is building a base off the floor of a 65% collapse from $66.74 to $23.56, and three of the last four swings have been higher. Today it closed at $29.96, right after a three-outside-up candle off the 50-day at $29.36, which was retested and held today, one session after the 20-day at $28.00 did the same. The support zone from $28.12 to $28.83 and the 10-day at $28.24 sit just beneath. The bigger picture still argues caution: the 200-day at $35.45 is falling, price is only 45% of the way to its $66.00 52-week high, and the weekly swing high at $30.27 is the first lid, barely above.

Momentum has quietly turned. MACD crossed above zero on Oct 20 and is above its signal line with the gap widening, RSI firmed to 59 from 58, and there is a hidden bullish divergence on MACD and on money flow. Volume is light, 0.65× normal today and 0.66× over ten sessions, so this is drift, not demand. Holders since the Aug 6 earnings report average $28.69 and are back in profit, and the spring on Aug 7 marks where sellers ran out. Revenue grew 10.6%, though profit fell to $55.3M from $99.9M. The weekly trend still points down while the hourly turned up. A coiled base with averages under it and a lid just overhead; the payoff is the push through $30.27.
prose.play: Buy $29.66 to $29.96 now. Target $33.31, the bottom of the resistance zone, by Nov 2; a daily close under $29.36, the 50-day, ends the trade.

story: City Holding added 0.9% to $142.10 on volume of 1.28× normal but printed a pin bar right at its 50-day at $142.90, the average it lost on Sep 21, so the first try failed and a retest of support comes next. That support is tight: the 20-day at $140.70 held its retest on Oct 19, the 10-day sits at $140.55, and a support line runs near $140.90. The spring on Oct 1 that undercut the 40-day low and recovered marks the floor of the base, and the 200-day at $130.70 is well below. Above, the resistance zone from $141.80 to $143.20 is the first hurdle.

The bands sit in the narrowest fifth of the year, a squeeze that already released on volume, and ADX at 14 says the next trend is just starting. RSI rose to 53 from 48 and MACD crossed up over its signal line on Oct 15 while still below zero, an early turn, with a fresh daily buy mark. Holders since the Jul 22 earnings report average $142.62 and are slightly under water, which explains the stall at the 50-day. The six-month gain of 13% tops 74% of stocks, and the 52-week high of $148.99 is the objective, with the failed upthrust of Aug 14 just under it the last obstacle.

prose.headline: Campbell's: sell a failed rally into $21.26, target $19.10 by Nov 6; a daily close above $21.47 kills the short.
story: Campbell's has spent most of the year in a weekly downtrend, a 42% slide from the $32.04 52-week high to the $18.60 low, and it has won back only a sliver of that. Today's 2.6% pop to $19.86 reclaimed the 20-day at $19.53. The bounce is now walking into a ceiling it already failed at: the 50-day at $21.26 is falling, with a resistance zone from $21.21 to $21.60 and the weekly swing high at $21.47 stacked on it. The 200-day at $22.68 and the 10-month line at $22.67 both slope down, and the down gap from the Sep 3 earnings report is still unfilled at $23.72.

The bounce has little behind it. Volume was only 0.69× normal on the up day, the accumulation line carries a bearish divergence, and ADX at 30 says the dominant trend is still the decline. RSI firmed to 48 from 42 and MACD crossed above its signal line on Oct 12, but MACD remains below zero. Holders since the Sep 3 earnings report average $20.37 and are underwater, so every rally into that level meets supply. Over three months the stock trails the S&P 500 by 12.1 points and its consumer staples sector by 13.2 points, and revenue fell 4.4% even as profit rose to $124.0M. The desk has its own long order queued for weakness, the opposite of this card. A light-volume rally into a falling 50-day is the short.

prose.headline: Donnelley Financial: buy the neckline retest at $51.31, next stop $53.81 by Oct 29; wrong under $50.75.
story: Donnelley Financial completed a double bottom on Oct 16 by clearing its neckline at $51.31, and the Oct 19 retest of that line held. It closed at $52.51, having won back 81% of the drop from the $56.26 52-week high to the $36.11 low. The averages are all rising and stacked underneath: the 10-day at $50.45, the 20-day at $49.25, the 50-day at $48.73 and the 200-day at $47.10. A support line near $48.17 and the busiest price at $48.30 make the deeper floor. Overhead, the weekly swing high at $53.56 and the resistance zone from $53.32 to $54.64 are where today's gap higher stalled.

That stall is the reason to let it come back to the neckline. The session gapped up and left a gravestone doji with a pin-bar rejection into resistance, closing near its low. The trend underneath is sound: MACD is above zero and its signal line with a confirmed bullish divergence on the MACD momentum bars, RSI is at 65, and volume is running 1.22× normal today and 1.15× over ten sessions. Insider buying is on the books, holders since the Jul 30 earnings report average $48.56, and the stock is 9.9 points ahead of its financials sector over three months. October has been a weak month for it, and price is already 2.4 daily ranges above the 50-day. A completed base; the best fill is back on the line it broke.

story: FTI Consulting gained 1.7% to $150.68 but on light volume of 0.72× normal, ending with a spinning top and wick rejection at its 20-session high. Just above, the weekly swing high at $153.67 and the resistance zone from $152.70 to $154.00 cap the move, and the 38.2% Fibonacci retrace of the drop sits at $152.10. A pullback has good landing spots: the volume-weighted price since the Jul 31 earnings report at $145.73 and the 50-day at $145.50, which held its retest on Oct 19. Below them sit the 10-day at $142.40, the unfilled gap from Oct 15 at $140.44, and the 20-day at $138.70.

Momentum is building: MACD crossed above zero on Oct 19 and is above its signal line with the gap widening, RSI rose to 63 from 60, and ADX at 20 marks a trend forming. On-balance volume rises with price. This is still a rebound in a longer decline, though, with a six-month loss of 19%, the 200-day at $160.40 falling and the 10-month average at $159.25 overhead, and the accumulation line has not confirmed the latest high. The spring on Sep 25 under the 40-day low marked the bottom. The trade is the bounce back to the weekly swing high from the earnings price.

prose.headline: Frontdoor: buy the 20-day at $76.77 on a pullback, $85.32 the target by Nov 6; out under $76.05.
story: Frontdoor reclaimed its 50-day at $79.78 today and closed at $80.48, on a trend of higher highs and higher lows that has added 30% in six months. The 20-day at $76.77 was reclaimed on Oct 15, the 10-day at $78.70 is turning up, and the 200-day at $68.38 rises far below. Price is sitting on the busiest price of the past month at $79.81, inside a high-volume range from $76.05 to $85.32. The support zone from $77.63 to $79.13 lies directly under it, and the 38.2% Fibonacci level at $76.26 sits near the bottom of the range. The spring on Sep 24 and a support line near $72.91 hold the deeper floor.

Volume came in heavy at 1.37× normal, but the bar closed near its low as a gravestone doji with a pin-bar rejection at a recent swing high, so the first push met sellers. Underneath, the gauges are firm: MACD crossed above zero on Oct 19 and sits above its signal line with the gap widening, RSI rose to 57 from 56, on-balance volume is rising with price, and the accumulation line shows a hidden bullish divergence. Over three months the stock is 8.8 points ahead of the S&P 500 and 10.4 points ahead of its sector, profit rose to $125.0M from $111.0M, and holders since the Aug 6 earnings report average $79.95. The 52-week high at $93.43 is the bigger magnet. A clean uptrend that just needs a dip to the 20-day.

The support zone from $77.63 to $79.13 lies directly under it, and the 38.2% Fibonacci level at $76.26 sits near the bottom of the range. The spring on Sep 24 and a support line near $72.91 hold the deeper floor.

Volume came in heavy at 1.37× normal, but the bar closed near its low as a gravestone doji with a pin-bar rejection at a recent swing high, so the first push met sellers. Underneath, the gauges are firm: MACD crossed above zero on Oct 19 and sits above its signal line with the gap widening, RSI rose to 57 from 56, on-balance volume is rising with price, and the accumulation line shows a hidden bullish divergence. Over three months the stock is 8.8 points ahead of the S&P 500 and 10.4 points ahead of its sector, profit rose to $125.0M from $111.0M, and holders since the Aug 6 earnings report average $79.95. The 52-week high at $93.43 is the bigger magnet. A clean uptrend that just needs a dip to the 20-day.

Pullback entry at the 20-day, $76.77, by Oct 23, filling to $78.01. The target is $85.32, the top of the high-volume range, by Nov 6; a daily close under $76.05, the bottom of the range, voids the call.

prose.headline: ZoomInfo: buy the 20-day at $3.83 by Oct 23, aiming at $4.33 by Nov 2; wrong under $3.77.
story: ZoomInfo jumped 4.3% to $4.10, pulling away from a tight cluster of support that makes the pullback entry easy to define. The 20-day at $3.83 was reclaimed on Oct 19 and the 50-day at $3.92 held its retest today. The 10-day sits at $3.90 and a support line runs near $3.77, framing the support zone from $3.83 to $3.96. Since the Aug 5 report, the average holder paid $3.95 and is now in the green. Overhead, the weekly swing high at $4.36 and the resistance zone from $4.33 to $4.40 are where the August upthrust failed, the natural first objective.

This is a base in a beaten-down stock: price is at only 33% of its 52-week high of $12.31, the six-month loss is 34%, and the 200-day at $5.02 is still falling, with the open gap from May 12 at $5.99 far above. Inside that base the turn is clear. MACD crossed above zero on Oct 15 and sits over its signal line, RSI rose to 58 from 53, and the daily chart printed a fresh buy mark. Relative strength leads the case, 37.5 points ahead of the S&P 500 and 39.5 points ahead of its sector over three months. ADX at 14 says the trend is young, so buy the dip, not the pop.

prose.headline: HOPE Bancorp: buy the pullback entry at $13.03, higher to the 50-day at $13.80 by Nov 4; out below $12.96.
story: HOPE Bancorp added 2.1% to $13.62 on volume of 1.20× normal and reclaimed its 20-day at $13.48. It closed right under the resistance zone from $13.64 to $13.80, where the falling 50-day and the weekly swing high at $13.81 meet. A first push into that wall usually fades, which sets up the entry lower down. The floor is well marked by the 10-day at $13.38 and the spring on Oct 1 that undercut the 40-day low and recovered. Below that sit the support zone from $12.96 to $13.06 and the rising 200-day at $12.73, with the 38.2% Fibonacci retrace at $12.76.

Momentum flipped this week. MACD crossed above its signal line on Oct 19 while still below zero, RSI jumped to 52 from 43, ADX at 26 shows a trend in force, and the daily chart printed a fresh buy mark. On-balance volume rises with price, though money flow and MACD have lagged the summer highs. Holders since the Jul 27 earnings report average $13.86 and are under water, the reason the 50-day is the objective rather than the 52-week high of $14.59. The six-month gain of 10% beats 71% of stocks. A low-risk dip buy back to the 50-day.

prose.headline: Hexcel: buy the halfway retrace at $86.28, upside to $95.14 by Nov 10; invalid on a daily close under $85.18.
story: Hexcel gave back 0.3% to $91.32 on heavy volume of 1.58× normal, and the bar was a gravestone doji with a pin-bar rejection right at the busiest price of the month, $91.72. That rejection is why the entry sits lower. The daily swings still step up, higher highs and higher lows since the spring on Sep 30, and the 50-day at $90.96 held its retest today just above the 200-day at $90.61. The halfway Fibonacci retrace of the whole run from $60.82 to $111.70 is $86.28, beside the 20-day at $86.53, which held its retest on Oct 14. The average buyer since the Oct 20, 2025 low sits at $86.17. That cluster is the buy.

The bigger picture is heavier. The weekly chart shows a topping 30-week average and bearish divergences on weekly RSI, MACD and the accumulation line, holders since the Jul 29 earnings report average $92.96 and are trapped, and the stock trails the S&P 500 by 17.2 points over three months in an industrials sector near the bottom of the map. The daily side argues back with ADX at 29, MACD above its signal line though still below zero, and RSI at 61. On-balance volume is rising, and profit is up to $49.3M from $13.5M on 8.0% revenue growth. The support zone from $88.43 to $89.88 and the confluence of swing lows from $82.25 to $83.05 frame the floor. A daily uptrend inside a tired weekly chart; buy it only at the halfway level.

story: Innoviva edged up 0.9% to $21.28 on light volume of 0.72× normal, sitting just above both averages it reclaimed on Oct 19: the 20-day at $20.90 and the 50-day at $20.99, with the 10-day at $21.03. The 50% Fibonacci retrace of the year's advance at $20.84 and the earnings price since the Aug 5 report at $20.94 sit in the same pocket, a dense floor, and a support line near $20.25 backs it. Above, the resistance zone from $21.17 to $21.69 and the weekly swing high at $21.51 hold the first push, and the upthrust over $21.70 on Oct 15 failed.

MACD crossed above zero on Oct 20 and sits over its signal line with the gap widening, RSI rose to 55 from 52, the daily chart printed a fresh buy mark, and the accumulation line and money flow both show hidden bullish divergences. ADX at 11 shows no trend yet, so this is a range trade from the floor to the 20-session high. The weekly chart is still in a decline, with the 200-day at $21.83 overhead, and the stock trails health care by 13.5 points over three months. The stock is at 85% of its 52-week high of $25.15. The averages are the buy.

prose.headline: J&J Snack Foods: buy now in the $81.27 to $81.82 zone, upside to $87.97 by Nov 2; wrong under $80.34.
story: Shares of J&J Snack Foods opened with a gap, rose 3.2% to $81.82 and closed near the high, right on top of the support zone from $80.34 to $81.69, so the entry is here rather than lower. The base under it is solid, with the 10-day at $80.05 and the 38.2% Fibonacci retrace at $80.24. Lower down, the 20-day at $78.90 held its retest on Oct 19, and a heavy-volume shelf from $77.43 to $78.75 sits on a support line near $77.36. The spring on Oct 1 that undercut the 40-day low and recovered marked the bottom. Price now sits at the 200-day at $81.84, with the 50-day at $82.96 and the weekly swing high at $83.16 the next hurdles.

RSI jumped to 57 from 47 and MACD is back above its signal line while still below zero, an early turn, and the daily chart printed a fresh buy mark. ADX at 13 says no trend yet, so the move has to build. Volume over ten sessions ran 1.20× normal, buyers stepping in at the lows. The weekly chart still lags, holders since the Aug 5 earnings report average $83.61 and are under water, and the stock sits at 83% of its 52-week high of $98.63. Consumer staples lead the sector map, and the resistance zone from $87.97 to $89.22 sits just over the deepest Fibonacci retrace at $87.26, the logical ceiling for this leg.

prose.headline: Cleveland-Cliffs is a buy at $13.65, upside to $14.94 by Oct 27; a close beneath $13.23 ends it.
story: Cleveland-Cliffs broke out of a symmetrical triangle on Oct 9 at $12.68 on volume and has won back two thirds of its fall from $16.70 to $7.73, gaining half in six months. Today it gave back 3.2% to $13.65, but the low found the support zone from $12.74 to $13.23 and left a pin-bar rejection and a dragonfly doji, a tri-star of indecision candles right on the shelf. The golden Fibonacci retrace sits at $13.27 inside that zone. Above, holders since the Oct 19 earnings report average $13.71 and the weekly swing high at $14.02 is the next lid, while the 20-day at $12.28 and the 50-day at $12.07 rise underneath.

The drop came on heavy volume, 2.96× normal, which is the risk, yet the close finished near the high of the bar and MACD carries a confirmed hidden bullish divergence. RSI eased to 62 from 67, MACD is above zero and its signal line with the gap widening, and the trend strength on ADX reads 20. The earnings report on Oct 19 showed revenue up 18.5% and profit of $152.0M against a $251.0M loss, with positive headlines behind it. Over three months the stock has beaten the S&P 500 by 41.5 points, even with its materials sector lagging. The weekly, daily and hourly charts all trend higher. A heavy shakeout that held the breakout shelf is a buy while the shelf holds.
prose.play: Buy $13.44 to $13.65 now. Target $14.94, the bottom of the resistance zone, by Oct 27; a daily close under $13.23, the top of the support zone, voids the call.

prose.headline: Dick's Sporting Goods: short a failed bounce at $147.47, target $139.32 by Oct 29, wrong over $148.83.
story: Dick's Sporting Goods is in a weekly downtrend that cut it from a $244.38 52-week high to a $120.20 low, and three of the last four swings have been lower. The October bounce reclaimed the 20-day at $136.60 and reached $143.08, but it is now pressing into the 50-day at $145.70, which has fallen 16.2% in a month. The short entry at the 20-session high of $147.47 and the weekly swing high at $148.83 sit right on top of it. The 200-day at $195.40 and the 10-month line at $189.36 are far above and falling, and the down gap from the Aug 25 earnings report is still open at $175.65.

The bounce is a counter-trend move into heavy supply. RSI eased to 55 from 57, MACD is above its signal line but still below zero, and the accumulation line carries a bearish divergence while volume runs at an ordinary 1.03× normal. Over three months the stock trails the S&P 500 by 34.8 points and its sector by 33.2 points. There are real arguments on the other side: insider buying, revenue up 53.2%, holders since the Aug 25 report in profit at $132.53, and bullish divergences on money flow and the MACD momentum bars. October has also been a weak month for the name. The desk's own strategies bought it today on the long side; this card takes the other side at the falling 50-day.

prose.headline: ADM is breaking down: short $80.46 for $77.17 by Oct 27, wrong on a daily close over $82.09.
story: Archer-Daniels-Midland slipped under both its 20-day at $81.32 and its 50-day at $82.27 on Oct 19, and the support line that carried the summer advance is already broken. The close at $80.46 sits on the busiest price of the past month, $80.48, inside a high-volume range that runs from $79.34 to $85.50, so the stock is resting on its last heavy-traffic shelf. Above it, holders since the Aug 4 earnings report average $82.09 and are underwater, and the weekly swing high at $82.95 caps any lift. The 52-week high of $88.75 from Sep 10 is the last swing high, while the 200-day at $75.83 still rises underneath.

prose.headline: Doximity: buy the pullback to $30.59, target $34.22 by Nov 4; the trade is wrong on a close under $29.62.
story: Doximity gapped up 6.0% to $33.35 today on volume of 1.62× normal, the latest leg of an uptrend built on higher highs and higher lows since the breakaway gap of Aug 7, which is still unfilled at $22.43. The 20-day at $28.94 and the 50-day at $27.01 are rising fast, both above the 200-day at $25.97. The stock has won back part of its 77% collapse from $73.92 to $17.15 and still sits at only 47% of its $71.37 52-week high, so the room overhead is large. The next marker is the busiest price of the past month at $34.22, then the weekly swing high at $35.43.

The trend is as strong as it gets on this chart: ADX at 42, RSI up to 74 from 68, MACD above zero and its signal line with the gap widening, and hidden bullish divergences on the stochastic and the accumulation line. Over three months it has beaten the S&P 500 by 59.9 points, and its six-month gain of 38% tops 91% of stocks. Holders since the Aug 6 earnings report average $27.59. The flaw is distance: price is stretched 4.7 daily ranges above the 50-day, the most of its past year, and the hourly chart has already flashed a sell mark. Revenue grew 7.3% while profit fell to $24.3M from $53.3M. A leader on a heavy gap, too extended to chase; the 10-day is the place to own it.

prose.headline: monday.com: buy a pullback into $96.52, target $119.07 by Nov 13; dead below $94.79.
story: monday.com jumped 8.0% to $100.86 on volume of 1.55× normal, gapping through the resistance line that had capped its base and closing near the high with a three-inside-up pattern on top of the support zone from $96.52 to $99.40. The base underneath is wide: the spring on Sep 30 marked the low, a support line near $74.68 has three touches, the 20-day at $85.65 held its retest on Oct 14 and the 50-day at $88.85 held its own on Oct 19. The old high-volume range tops at $94.79, the line this breakout must keep. Just overhead, the weekly swing high at $102.00 is the first test, and the stock is still only at 48% of its $210.49 52-week high.

Momentum has turned decisively: RSI rose to 65 from 58 and MACD is above zero and its signal line with the gap widening. Some gauges lag the move, with divergences on on-balance volume, money flow and the MACD momentum bars, and ADX at 13 says the trend is young. The six-month gain of 49% tops 94% of stocks, and the stock is 33.6 points ahead of the S&P 500 over three months. Price is stretched 2.3 daily ranges above the 50-day, more than 96% of its past year, right after a big gap, so the first dip into the support zone is the better fill. Three of the desk's strategies are long it now. A base breakout on volume with a lot of room overhead.

prose.headline: Devon: buy the dip to $49.16, $51.49 target by Oct 29; under $48.78 the trade is off.
story: Devon backed off 1.1% to $50.38 today after an engulfing outside bar at the weekly swing high of $50.84, the first real push back in a month. The swing structure is constructive, three of the last four swings higher, and the averages are stacked: the 10-day at $49.54, the 20-day at $48.48, the 50-day at $48.22 and the 200-day at $45.38. The busiest price of the past month at $49.16 sits just below, inside a high-volume range from $46.87 to $50.25. Under that, a support zone from $47.82 to $48.65 and a support line near $47.04 with three touches behind it guard the trend. The 52-week high of $52.71 is 96% reached.

Momentum is cooling, not cracking. RSI eased to 59 from 63, MACD is above zero and its signal line but the gap is narrowing, and a hidden bullish divergence on the MACD momentum bars hints at more to come. Volume is ordinary at 0.92× normal. The fundamentals are excellent, revenue up 73.1% and profit at $1,911.0M against $899.0M, energy leads the sector map, and holders since the Aug 4 earnings report average $47.80, in profit. The weekly chart is starting to look heavy, with the 30-week average flattening, so the trade is aimed at the resistance zone, not beyond it. A strong stock taking a breather at a lid; buy it at the busiest price.

prose.headline: Freshpet is a buy at $66.05, target $69.58 by Oct 26, wrong if it closes under $64.68.
story: Freshpet is sitting exactly where a base usually gets challenged. At $66.05 it is on the halfway Fibonacci retrace of its 46% slide from $86.00 to $46.45. The last bar was a pin-bar rejection, a doji and an outside bar right at the support zone from $63.59 to $65.01. The 10-day at $65.85 is just under price, the 200-day at $63.74 and the 20-day at $62.39 are below, and the spring on Sep 29 marked the bottom of the move. The flaw is that price slipped under the 50-day at $66.47 on Oct 19, and that same level is the weekly swing high, so a close back above it is the first job.

The momentum gauges side with the bounce. RSI and the MACD momentum bars show bullish divergences, including on the weekly RSI, and MACD is above zero and its signal line, although the gap is narrowing and RSI eased to 57 from 58. Volume was light at 0.78× normal today. Holders since the Aug 5 earnings report average $67.06 and are slightly underwater, and the busiest price of the past month at $72.64 sits overhead inside a high-volume range that tops at $75.55. Revenue grew 15.5% and profit rose to $19.5M, the stock is 13.2 points ahead of its sector over three months, and the desk's own strategies bought it today. A base holding its halfway level is a buy with a tight line.
prose.play: Buy $65.46 to $66.05 now. The target is $69.58, the 20-session high, by Oct 26; a daily close under $64.68 voids the call.

prose.headline: Intuit: buy the pullback to the $315.11 earnings VWAP, objective $340.20 by Oct 29; wrong under $311.20.
story: Intuit gapped up 3.0% to $335.29 today, the latest step in a base that started with the spring on Sep 29 off a 63% collapse from the $689.17 52-week high to $252.80. The 50-day at $321.00 held its retest on Oct 19, the 20-day at $296.50 held on Oct 8, and the 10-day at $313.80 is turning higher. Holders since the Aug 25 earnings report average $315.11 and are in profit, and the support zone from $303.50 to $311.20 sits under that. Overhead is busy: the busiest price of the month at $343.93 and the resistance zone from $340.20 to $350.90, then the falling 200-day at $372.20 and two unfilled gaps from May.

The momentum turn is real. RSI rose to 65 from 61, MACD crossed above zero on Oct 16 and is well above its signal line, and RSI and the MACD momentum bars carry bullish divergences on the daily and weekly charts. The gap came on ordinary volume, 0.72× normal today and 1.00× over ten sessions, so it was not a crowd chasing it. Profit rose to $3,064.0M on 10.4% revenue growth, positive headlines are in the flow, and the stock is 15.0 points ahead of the S&P 500 over three months. The desk's own strategies already hold it. The flaw is the monthly picture, still under a falling 10-month line at $360.77. A base turning up into resistance; buy the dip to the earnings VWAP.

prose.headline: Centene's double bottom breakout: a dip to $69.03 is the entry, $79.80 the target by Nov 18; out under $68.27.
story: Centene finished a double bottom and a rectangle in one move, breaking out on Oct 15 at $69.63, and today's 3.2% gain to $70.81 left it 99% of the way to its 52-week high of $71.21. Today's dip back to the breakout level was a retest, and the close came off the session high right at the support zone from $69.03 to $69.96. Below that, the 10-day at $68.00 rises. A cluster of five levels between $64.16 and $65.48 stacks up with the 50-day at $65.54 and the 20-day at $65.28, both of which held their retests earlier this month. A support line near $63.40 and a rising 200-day at $54.43 complete the floor.

Momentum is clean. RSI rose to 66 from 60, MACD is above zero and its signal line, and the MACD momentum bars printed a confirmed bullish divergence before the breakout. Volume is ordinary at 0.93× normal, and on-balance volume has not kept pace, which is the soft spot. The six-month gain of 81% puts it ahead of 97% of stocks, holders since the Jul 27 earnings report average $64.99, and profit swung to $1,091.0M from a $253.0M loss on 9.9% revenue growth. Health care leads the sector map, and the weekly, daily and hourly trends all point up. The weekly swing high at $71.66 is the last hurdle before the measured move opens. That is a fresh base breakout getting its first test.

prose.headline: Coty: buy a dip to $3.11, next stop $3.38 by Nov 2; done on a close below $3.04.
story: Coty turned its swings around this autumn: after the spring on Sep 21 shook out the lows, price cleared the last swing high and now trades at $3.22, sitting above the halfway retrace of its long slide at $3.15. The 20-day at $2.84 and the 50-day at $2.78 both held their retests on Oct 5 and Oct 8, and the 10-day at $3.00 is rising. The old high-volume range from $2.62 to $2.86 is now well below as a floor. Right under price, the support zone from $3.04 to $3.11 caught the last bar, which printed a pin-bar rejection and a hanging man. The resistance zone from $3.38 to $3.49 is the next ceiling.

Price is moving easily on light volume, 0.69× normal over ten sessions, which says little supply stands in the way. RSI is hot at 75 and MACD sits above zero and its signal line, ADX at 30 confirms a trending market, and a hidden bullish divergence backs the move. The six-month gain of 37% beats 91% of stocks, and the stock has outrun SPY by 28.9 points in a month. The weak spots: price is stretched 3.7 daily ranges above the 50-day, more than 95% of its past year, and the loss is still $408.1M with revenue down 1.3%. Holders since the Aug 19 earnings report average $2.77 and sit in profit. A steady trend, too extended to chase, best bought at the support zone.
prose.play: Buy a pullback to $3.11, the 3-session low, by Oct 23, filling to $3.16. The target is $3.38, the bottom of the resistance zone, by Nov 2; a daily close under $3.04 voids the call.

Right under price, the support zone from $3.04 to $3.11 caught the last bar, which printed a pin-bar rejection and a hanging man. The resistance zone from $3.38 to $3.49 is the next ceiling.

Price is moving easily on light volume, 0.69× normal over ten sessions, which says little supply stands in the way. RSI is hot at 75 and MACD sits above zero and its signal line, ADX at 30 confirms a trending market, and a hidden bullish divergence backs the move. The six-month gain of 37% beats 91% of stocks, and the stock has outrun SPY by 28.9 points in a month. The weak spots: price is stretched 3.7 daily ranges above the 50-day, more than 95% of its past year, and the loss is still $408.1M with revenue down 1.3%. Holders since the Aug 19 earnings report average $2.77 and sit in profit. A steady trend, too extended to chase, best bought at the support zone.
Buy a pullback to $3.11, the 3-session low, by Oct 23, filling to $3.16. The target is $3.38, the bottom of the resistance zone, by Nov 2; a daily close under $3.04 voids the call.

prose.headline: Gartner's triangle breakout is a buy back at $204.30, aiming for $253.37 by Nov 25; finished below $201.80.
story: A 5.7% gap higher to $219.64 on volume of 1.97× normal put Gartner further into a breakout today, the move out of an ascending triangle that cleared $202.93 on Oct 15 and held its retest on Oct 19. The same level turned back an upthrust on Oct 1, so the breakout settled a real fight. The stock has now won back 70% of its slide from the $261.10 52-week high to $124.20. Underneath, the 10-day at $199.92, the 20-day at $192.70 and the 50-day at $189.70 all rise, and both longer averages held their retests on Oct 8. The support zone from $201.80 to $204.30 sits on top of the old breakout line, the natural place for a retest.

The momentum is broad and strong. ADX at 31 marks a trending market, RSI jumped to 71 from 65, MACD is above zero and its signal line with the gap widening, and MACD, on-balance volume and the accumulation line all show hidden bullish divergences. The six-month gain of 38% beats 92% of stocks, and the stock is 63.4 points ahead of the S&P 500 over three months even with its sector lagging. Holders since the Aug 4 earnings report average $188.61 and are well in profit. The only problem is distance: price is stretched 3.7 daily ranges above the 50-day, more than 94% of its past year, after a heavy gap. A confirmed breakout worth owning, at the breakout shelf rather than the gap.

story: Eli Lilly gapped up 3.5% to $1,283.66 on volume of 1.35× normal, landing 98% of the way to its 52-week high of $1,311.75 with the weekly swing high at $1,292.65 directly overhead. The trend is textbook: higher highs and higher lows, the 50-day at $1,182.00 reclaimed on Oct 14 in the same session the 20-day at $1,188.00 held its retest, the 10-day at $1,212.81 rising, and the 200-day at $1,082.00 far below. The six-month gain of 42% tops 92% of stocks. The fundamentals are enormous, revenue up 47.7% and profit at $7,095.0M against $5,661.0M, with positive headlines and holders since the Aug 5 earnings report averaging $1,187.13. Health care leads the sector map. A gap into the weekly swing high is not where to pay up, and the room to the next measured target only opens from lower down; the 3-session low is the entry.

story: Molina broke out of a descending triangle on Oct 12 at $200.16 on volume, held the retest the next day, and today ran 4.5% to $219.72 on volume of 1.51× normal. The upthrust of Oct 14 over $214.36 failed at first, but today's close sits above that level after a three-inside-up pattern at the support zone from $213.20 to $216.00. The 50-day at $200.10 was reclaimed on Oct 12 and the 20-day at $198.10 held its retest the same day. Below, six separate levels cluster from $199.30 to $204.20, the busiest price of the month at $199.27 among them, a thick floor under any pullback.

RSI rose to 68 from 61 after a confirmed bullish divergence, and MACD is above zero and its signal line with the gap widening. Volume has been heavy, 1.29× normal over ten sessions, on-balance volume is rising, and the spring on Oct 2 marked the low of the base. The six-month gain of 46% beats 93% of stocks, and the 52-week high of $244.89 is the 120-session high and the objective. The weak spots are the business, with profit down to $60.0M from $255.0M and revenue off 4.8%, and the stock trails its health care sector by 13.7 points over three months. Anyone who bought after the Jul 22 report is above water, with that group's average cost at $200.92. A confirmed breakout to buy on the first dip.

prose.headline: Perrigo: buy the 20-day at $15.09 on the dip, upside $16.79 by Nov 2; out under $14.90.
story: Perrigo closed at $16.17, up 0.5% on light volume of 0.73× normal, but the day ended with a pin bar and close near the low at its 20-session high, a sign the stock needs to rest. The rest has an obvious landing spot. The 20-day at $15.09, which held its retest on Oct 9, sits on top of the support zone from $14.90 to $15.15, and the 10-day is at $15.62. The 50-day at $14.37 and the busiest price of the month at $14.24 are the deeper floor, and the Aug 5 breakaway gap that launched this trend is still open far below. The swings have climbed with higher highs and higher lows, and price closed over the last swing high at $15.69.

Few charts have this kind of relative strength: the stock is 51.5 points ahead of the S&P 500 and 41.7 points ahead of health care over three months, and the six-month gain of 38% beats 91% of stocks. ADX at 28 confirms a real trend, and hidden bullish divergences on the MACD momentum bars, stochastic and accumulation line show dips being bought. MACD is above zero and its signal line but the gap is narrowing, so momentum is cooling into a pullback. RSI sits at 64, well short of overbought. The business swung to a $74.5M profit from an $8.4M loss, and holders since the Aug 5 earnings report average $14.24. The 52-week high of $22.02 leaves plenty of room above.

prose.headline: Blackbaud: long a dip into $50.58 aiming for $61.18 by Nov 30; finished on a close under $48.78.
story: Blackbaud closed at $53.57 with about two thirds of its slide from the $70.71 52-week high to the $25.58 low already recovered, sitting on the golden Fibonacci retrace at $53.47. The swings turned this autumn: the spring on Sep 30 shook out the lows, and price has since cleared the last swing high and held retests of both the 20-day and the 50-day. Those two averages sit together near $45.71 and $45.77 above a support line near $45.19. The 10-day at $48.84 is rising fast, and the top of the high-volume range at $48.78 is the line in the sand. A rising wedge is forming, so the run is steep.

Momentum is strong and running hot. RSI sits at 80, MACD is above zero and its signal line, the trend strength reads 29 on ADX, and on-balance volume is climbing with price on 1.17× normal volume over ten sessions. The catch is stretch: price is 4.5 daily ranges above the 50-day, more than 90% of its past year, and the last bar was a spinning top with a wick rejection at the 20-session high. Over three months it has outrun the S&P 500 by 70.4 points, holders since the Jul 29 earnings report average $45.10, and profit rose to $35.4M from $26.5M. The weekly trend has turned up, with the weekly swing high at $61.18 as the next magnet. Strong trend, poor price to chase; let it come back to the 10-day area.

prose.headline: Paylocity: buy the dip to $164.96 for $173.81 by Oct 30; the call is void below $163.27.
story: Paylocity is the strongest chart in this group. It gapped up 2.3% to $170.06, closing over its last swing high at $161.90 and sitting 99% of the way to its 52-week high of $171.43, with the weekly swing high at $173.81 the next level. The upthrust that failed at $159.26 on Sep 1 is now well behind it. Every average points up and sits far below: the 10-day at $159.70, the 20-day at $152.00, the 50-day at $150.40 and the 200-day at $125.40. Price is 4.5 daily ranges above the 50-day, more than 96% of its past year, so chasing the open is poor value.

The trend gauges are pinned: ADX at 34 with buyers in firm control, RSI climbing to 80 from 76, and MACD above zero and its signal line. The six-month gain of 64% beats 96% of stocks and the stock is 37.9 points ahead of the S&P 500 over three months. Revenue grew 10.5% and profit rose to $111.2M from $91.5M, while holders since the Aug 4 earnings report average $149.50 and sit comfortably in profit. Hidden bullish divergences on the MACD momentum bars and money flow show dips getting absorbed. Overbought leaders tend to pause rather than reverse, so a 2-session low is the place to step in.

prose.headline: Baxter is a buy at $24.51, targeting $25.97 by Oct 28; a daily close under $24.01 breaks it.
story: Baxter has climbed a third in six months on higher highs and higher lows, and today's 1.9% dip did its work at a level that matters. Price closed at $24.51, right on the 38.2% Fibonacci retrace of the run from $15.73 to $30.00 and a hair above the busiest price of the month at $24.26, where the session left a wick rejection. The 20-day at $24.21 was retested and held, the support line near $24.23 is intact, and the support zone at $23.55 to $24.01 sits just below. The cost of the day was the 50-day: price slipped under it at $24.89, which is also the nearest weekly swing high, so that is the first lid.

The selling was loud, 2.18× normal volume, yet price held the shelf, and both RSI and MACD carry hidden bullish divergences while the accumulation line agrees. prose.headline: Chord Energy: buy the pullback to $141.70, objective $157.06 by Nov 6, stop on a daily close under $140.10.
story: Chord Energy ran to within reach of its 52-week high of $157.06 and today got slapped back 1.5% to $152.22, an engulfing outside bar right at the weekly swing high of $153.00. The trend underneath is fine. The 50-day at $143.90 held a retest on Oct 15, the 20-day at $141.70 held one on Oct 9, and the 200-day at $128.80 is rising. A support line near $138.50 and the support zone topping out at $140.10 sit below, with the busiest price of the past month at $137.59. That is a stack of floors between $137.59 and $143.90, and the pullback has room to reach the top of it.

Turnover on the reversal was 1.42× normal, so sellers showed up in size, and MACD and the accumulation line both carry a divergence against the last high. RSI eased to 63 from 68, and MACD is still above zero and its signal line with the gap narrowing, so momentum is cooling rather than breaking. The business carries it: revenue grew 84.0% and profit swung to $525.2M from a $389.9M loss, energy leads the sector map, and holders since the Oct 19 earnings report average $153.18, slightly under water, which explains today's selling. The weekly, daily and hourly trends all point up. That is a leader taking a breath after a hard day; the 20-day is where to step in, not here.

prose.headline: Coca-Cola: buy the dip to $90.55 and ride it to $94.10 by Nov 3; the long is wrong under $89.84.
story: Coca-Cola completed a double bottom on Oct 16 by clearing $92.49, and today's retest of that line held, leaving the stock at $93.49, 99% of the way to its 52-week high of $94.10. There is no weekly swing high above it on the chart, so the old high is the only ceiling. The averages are stacked in order and rising: the 10-day at $90.61, then the 20-day at $88.73 and the 50-day at $88.70, which were retested and reclaimed together on Oct 9, and the 200-day at $81.20. The top of the high-volume range at $89.84 is the floor of this leg, with the busiest price at $87.93 and a support line near $86.28 underneath.

For a defensive name this is an unusually strong trend. ADX reads 25, MACD is above zero and its signal line, on-balance volume rises with price, and the hourly chart printed a fresh buy mark. RSI sits at 72 and has not confirmed the latest high, a divergence to respect, and price is stretched 3.3 daily ranges above the 50-day, more than 84% of its past year. The business is firing: revenue grew 12.1%, profit reached $3,924.0M, headlines are positive, and holders since the Jul 28 earnings report average $88.56, with that report's breakaway gap still open below. Consumer staples lead the sector map, and the stock is 10.8 points ahead of the S&P 500 over three months. Own it on a shallow dip into the 10-day.

prose.headline: Metallus: buy the 50-day at $19.85, target $21.36 by Oct 30; wrong below $19.55.
story: Metallus has climbed on higher highs and higher lows since its September low and closed at $20.62, down 0.9% after a spinning top with a wick rejection at the top of the high-volume range. The averages are tightly bunched underneath: the 10-day at $20.36, the 20-day at $19.91, which held its retest on Oct 9, the 50-day at $19.85, which held its retest on Oct 15, and the 200-day at $19.08. The busiest price of the past month sits at $19.55, right under the 50-day, and a support line near $18.82 is the deeper floor. Overhead, the weekly swing high at $20.95 and a resistance zone from $20.90 to $21.32 are the lid.

Momentum is resting. RSI eased to 57 from 60 and MACD is above zero and its signal line with the gap narrowing, while the hourly chart flashed a sell mark, so the near-term drift is down toward the averages. The accumulation line and money flow show hidden bullish divergences, on-balance volume rises with price, and volume is ordinary at 0.88× normal. The business is improving: revenue grew 12.0% and profit rose to $8.9M from $3.7M, and holders since the Aug 3 earnings report average $20.09. The stock is 9.9 points ahead of its industrials sector over three months, and the desk's strategy bought it today. The 52-week high of $22.58 is the bigger target. A tight cluster of averages is the buy point.

prose.headline: Becton Dickinson: buy the pullback to $184.40 for a run to $195.30 by Nov 4; wrong below $182.80.
story: Becton Dickinson is pressing its 52-week high of $195.99 after a 1.6% gain to $193.80, clearing the last swing high on a clean run of higher highs and higher lows. The 20-day and the 50-day both sit at $184.40 and both were retested and held on Oct 9, the day MACD crossed up, and the 200-day at $164.50 is far below and rising. Under the averages, the high-volume range runs from $175.70 to $188.30 with the busiest price at $180.25, so the floor is thick. The last candles printed a hammer and a morning star, buyers stepping in on every dip.

What stands out is how easily price is moving: volume ran only 0.69× normal today and 0.89× over ten sessions, effort small and progress large, which says little supply is left in the way. RSI rose to 65 from 62 and MACD is above zero and its signal line with a steady gap, though RSI has not confirmed the new high, a divergence worth respecting. Holders since the Aug 6 earnings report average $183.51 and are in profit. Over three months the stock is 23.6 points ahead of the S&P 500 and 13.7 points ahead of its health care sector, though profit slipped to $377.0M from $574.0M on 5.4% revenue growth. Price is stretched 2.3 daily ranges above the 50-day, so the averages are the better place to own it.

prose.headline: BlackRock is a buy on a dip to $1,070.49, objective $1,136.26 by Nov 3; out below $1,062.79.
story: BlackRock has won back 70% of its drop from $1,220.00 to $917.40 and now trades at $1,128.68, 95% of the way to its 52-week high of $1,187.17. The 50-day at $1,106.00 was reclaimed on Oct 15 in the same session the 20-day held its retest, and the deepest Fibonacci retrace level at $1,104.00 sits right with it. Lower down, the busiest price of the month at $1,070.49 is the shelf to buy, with the 200-day at $1,062.00 and a support line near $1,050.00 underneath. Every timeframe from weekly to hourly points up.

Today was the warning shot. Volume hit 2.27× normal on a 0.4% gain, but the candle closed near its low after a wick rejection at the top of the high-volume range, so sellers met that heavy turnover head on. Momentum is otherwise firm: MACD is above zero and its signal line, RSI sits at 61, and on-balance volume is rising with price. The Oct 14 earnings report brought 30.6% revenue growth and profit of $1,914.0M, and holders since then average $1,115.37, still in profit. Negative headlines and a financials sector that lags the tape explain the stall. The spring on Sep 16, a flush under support that was bought back within three sessions, is the low this trend is built on. That is strength resting, and the busiest price is where it reloads.

prose.headline: Dollar General: buy support at $130.00 by Oct 23, measured target $147.20 by Nov 13; under $127.19 it fails.
story: Dollar General has rebuilt itself into a base after the spring on Oct 2 flushed the lows, and it now sits at $134.19, right on the 38.2% Fibonacci level of the whole run from $95.11 to $158.20. The close cleared the last swing high, and the old resistance line from the summer is broken and below. Both the 20-day at $125.30 and the 50-day at $124.80 were retested and held on Oct 14. The 10-day at $129.08 leads them up, and the support zone from $130.00 to $131.80 is the first shelf. Beneath that sits the whole high-volume range from $118.79 to $127.19, with the busiest price at $122.99 and a support line near $119.80.

Today was a pause, not a reversal. The bar left a gravestone doji with a pin-bar rejection right at the weekly swing high of $135.46, on light volume of 0.65× normal, so nobody pushed it down either. MACD is above zero and its signal line, RSI sits at 65, and the accumulation line and money flow both show hidden bullish divergences. Profit rose to $550.3M from $411.4M on 5.2% revenue growth, holders since the Aug 27 earnings report average $126.01, and consumer staples lead the sector map with the stock 8.7 points ahead of the S&P 500 over three months. The 52-week high of $158.23 is the long-range magnet. A base turning into a trend; buy it on the shelf, not into the lid.
prose.play: Bids belong at $130.00, the bottom of the support zone, on a pullback by Oct 23, with fills up to $131.91. The objective is $147.20, the measured move past the highs, by Nov 13; a daily close under $127.19, the top of the high-volume range, voids the call.

story: DiamondRock closed at $13.79, up 2.5% and a few cents from its 52-week high of $13.88, with no weekly swing high left on the chart above it. The structure underneath is a staircase: the 20-day at $12.74 was reclaimed on Oct 8, the 50-day at $12.51 held its retest on Oct 12, and the 200-day at $11.12 is rising. The 10-day at $13.03 is the nearest average, and the old high-volume range from $12.15 to $12.81, with the busiest price at $12.38, is now a floor well below. A support line near $12.04 frames the deepest level the trend has to hold.

Volume has run heavy at 1.39× normal over ten sessions, and ADX at 27 marks a real trend. RSI rose to 74 from 70, and MACD is above zero and its signal line with the gap widening. Two things argue for patience: price is stretched 3.8 daily ranges above the 50-day, more than 88% of its past year, and the accumulation line and money flow have diverged from the latest high. prose.headline: Employers Holdings: buy the retest of $50.15, target $52.59 by Oct 30; finished below $49.74.
story: Employers Holdings broke a descending triangle on Oct 14 at $49.60, the Oct 15 retest held, and the same move completed a double bottom. It closed at $51.70, up 0.9% and 98% of the way to its 52-week high of $52.60. The trouble is right overhead: the weekly swing high at $52.06 and a resistance zone from $51.90 to $52.75, where today's bar printed a pin-bar rejection and closed near its low inside the prior range. Underneath, the 10-day at $50.26 leads the 20-day at $49.21 and the 50-day at $49.07, both of which held their retests on Oct 8, and the 200-day at $45.59 is rising.

The pattern is sound and the timing is the issue. RSI rose to 71 from 68, MACD is above zero and its signal line with the gap widening, and on-balance volume is climbing, though volume itself is quiet at 0.85× normal and the accumulation line has diverged from price. The top of the high-volume range at $50.15 is the old ceiling turned floor, with the busiest price at $49.07 below it and a support line near $47.97 that has three touches. The spring on Sep 28 marked the low of the base. The business is flat, revenue down 10.6% and profit at $29.1M, but the stock is 5.3 points ahead of its financials sector over three months. A breakout that needs one more dip into the range top before it clears the high.

prose.headline: National Beverage: buy the support zone at $32.92, objective $35.47 by Nov 4; a close below $32.07 ends the long.
story: At $35.13, National Beverage has recovered two thirds of its fall from the $38.21 52-week high to the $28.97 low. Now it is up against the ceiling that matters: the weekly swing high at $35.57 and a resistance zone from $35.74 to $36.05. The base underneath is clean. The spring on Sep 11 marked the low, both the 20-day at $31.36 and the 50-day at $31.61 were reclaimed together on Oct 12, and price has since lifted back above the 200-day at $33.57. The support zone from $32.07 to $32.92 sits just above the 10-day at $32.88, and a support line near $29.22 anchors the base.

Momentum is broad: RSI rose to 72 from 70, MACD is above zero and its signal line, ADX at 28 confirms the trend, and RSI and MACD carry both regular and hidden bullish divergences. Insiders have been buying, short interest is heavy, and holders since the Sep 11 earnings report average $31.33 and are up comfortably. The stock is 10.0 points ahead of the S&P 500 over three months with consumer staples leading the sector map. The caution is stretch: price sits 3.9 daily ranges above the 50-day, more than 99% of its past year, on light volume of 0.76× normal today, and revenue was flat while profit slipped to $47.0M from $55.8M. A strong base into a lid; the support zone is where the risk is small.

prose.headline: Globant: long on a dip into $38.69, target $44.64 by Nov 5; a close below $37.73 ends it.
story: Globant is climbing out of a 62% collapse from its $72.10 52-week high to $27.56. It broke out of a symmetrical triangle on Oct 8 at $36.41, cleared the resistance line that capped the base, reclaimed the 50-day at $37.73 on Oct 15, and today added 3.8% to $41.65. The spring on Sep 29 marked the low, the 20-day at $36.48 held its retest on Oct 12, and the support zone from $37.61 to $38.69 is the first shelf below. Overhead, the 200-day at $43.07 is still falling, the 10-month line sits at $42.69, and the 38.2% Fibonacci level at $44.57 lines up with the 120-session high.

Price is moving easily on light volume, 0.79× normal today and 0.83× over ten sessions, which says little supply is in the way. RSI rose to 68 from 64, MACD is above zero and its signal line with the gap widening, and on-balance volume is rising with price. Over three months the stock has beaten the S&P 500 by 32.9 points, and heavy short interest can feed a squeeze. The caution flags are a hidden divergence on RSI and MACD, a six-month loss of 17%, and price stretched 2.2 daily ranges above the 50-day, more than 92% of its past year. A real base breakout running into a falling 200-day; buy it back at the support shelf.

prose.headline: Bumble at its 52-week high: buy $5.90 for $6.11 next by Nov 13, wrong under $5.84.
story: Bumble has more than doubled since a double bottom near $2.44 and a descending triangle breakout on Oct 12 at $2.84, and it now trades at $5.95 against a 52-week high of $5.98. The runaway gap from Oct 13 is still open and would fill at $3.97, the 20-day at $3.65 and the 50-day at $3.15 are far below, and the spring on Oct 8 marked the low of the whole move. Price is camped on the busiest price of the past month at $5.94, where the last bars printed a doji and a harami cross, a stall in a narrow range right at the top.

Volume has been heavy, 2.00× normal over ten sessions and 1.18× today, and ADX at 44 says this is a real trend. RSI is pinned at 90 and MACD is above zero and its signal line, though the gap is narrowing. On-balance volume has not kept up with price, and the stock is stretched 11.1 daily ranges above the 50-day, the most of its past year, so this is a name to buy only on a small dip, never on a gap up. It has outrun the S&P 500 by 108.8 points over three months while revenue shrank 15.2% and the loss narrowed to $110.1M from $253.7M. The weekly trend has turned up. Momentum rules here, and a tight pullback is the only entry.
